name: Amgen Inc.
reason: Big-biotech franchise facing a credible 5-year patent/biosimilar cliff (Prolia/Xgeva, Enbrel) and a binary obesity bet (MariTide vs GLP-1 incumbents); EBIT margin down from 44% to 29%, Horizon deal lifted net debt/EBITDA to 2.9x, and consensus EPS growth only ~5-6%.

name: American Homes 4 Rent
reason: Single-family rental REIT whose FFO growth (10% CAGR) came largely from external growth with shares up 5.8%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 5.1x, and consensus now expects FFO/EPS declines; rate- and housing-cycle dependent with no clear specialness.

name: Amkor Technology, Inc.
reason: Commodity-like semiconductor packaging/test (OSAT) with a 7% EBIT margin, EPS 0.48x its 2022 peak, flat 5y EPS (0.3% CAGR) and negative NTM FCF (-8.4% yield) from heavy capex - cyclical and capital-intensive.

name: Amneal Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
reason: Generic-heavy pharma with negative 10y avg ROIC (-5.1%), shares up 16.3%/yr, acquisitions 1.27x FCF, net debt/EBITDA 3.7x and EPS at 0.57x its 2015 level; FCF yield of 7.8% does not offset generic price erosion and government-channel reimbursement risk.

name: American Tower Corporation
reason: Tower moat is real, but growth was acquisition-led (acquisitions 1.21x FCF) at 6.1x net debt/EBITDA, AFFO/share grew only 4.9%/yr over 5y, and carrier consolidation/churn plus emerging-market FX keep the route to 7%+ EPS growth doubtful.

name: Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Inc.
reason: Life-science office REIT in a supply glut and biotech funding downturn: FFO fell in 2025 (-4.9%) with consensus forecasting further declines, shares up 9.1%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 6.1x; the 10.2% FCF yield reflects distress, not durable growth.

name: Ares Management Corporation
reason: High-quality alternative/private-credit manager (EPS CAGR 18.5%) but earnings depend on fundraising, credit cycles and realisations; shares up 10.4%/yr, consolidated net debt/EBITDA 6.25x and a ~123% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap make a 10-year forecast unreliable.

name: Ashland Inc.
reason: Specialty chemicals portfolio in perpetual restructuring: revenue down 10.3%/yr over 10y, EPS flat (-0.2% CAGR) and 0.59x its 2022 peak, EBIT margin 5.4% (9th pctile), net debt/EBITDA 3.2x; FCF yield driven by consensus recovery not recurring history.

name: Astrana Health Inc.
reason: Risk-bearing value-based care platform dependent on Medicare Advantage/Medicaid reimbursement and utilisation, growth bought via acquisitions (2.1x FCF) with shares up 25%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 5.2x, EPS at 0.28x its peak and EBIT margin 2.5%.

name: Atkore Inc
reason: Electrical conduit maker whose 2021-23 earnings boom was PVC/steel price-driven: EPS fell from $21.55 to $6.05 (0.28x peak) and EBIT margin from 31.6% to 8.3%, i.e. commodity-like pricing; the 8.9% FCF yield is real but cyclical.

name: Broadcom Inc.
reason: Exceptional operator/capital allocator, but growth has come from serial large acquisitions (VMware; shares up 5.6%/yr) and the forecast now hinges on custom AI accelerators concentrated in a few hyperscaler customers (consensus EPS +71%/+65%), which cannot be forecast 5-10 years out with confidence.

name: Avery Dennison Corporation
reason: Good but not special: pressure-sensitive materials (~2/3 of sales) are a cyclical pass-through business, 5y EPS CAGR only 6.1% with EBIT margin near its 10y high (91st pctile, 12.7%); RFID is a real secular driver but too small to make the whole special.

name: Armstrong World Industries, Inc.
reason: Ceiling duopoly with strong pricing (EPS CAGR 12.7%, ROIC 15%, net debt/EBITDA 0.9x), but EPS is at its 10y high with margin in the 91st pctile, demand is tied to commercial office renovation which faces structural hybrid-work uncertainty, and Architectural Specialties growth is acquisition-led.

name: American Express Company
reason: Closed-loop network with an affluent, spend-centric customer base and premium fee model (EPS CAGR 11.1% 10y, 32.5% 5y off the 2020 trough, shares down 3.6%/yr); credit exposure is real but underwriting has been conservative, and consensus ~14-15% EPS growth is plausible.

name: AutoZone, Inc.
reason: Dominant DIY/commercial auto-parts retailer with a non-discretionary, ageing-fleet demand driver, 41% avg ROIC and relentless buybacks (shares -5.7%/yr) producing 14.1% EPS CAGR with only one flat year; margin slightly below average (9th pctile) rather than at a peak and net debt/EBITDA 2.75x is manageable.

name: AZZ Inc.
reason: Galvanizing/coil-coating with zinc- and steel-linked economics, growth bought via the Precoat acquisition (acquisitions 1.29x FCF), EPS at its 10y high with EBIT margin at a 100th-pctile 16.3% - ordinary industrial at a cyclical high.

name: Boise Cascade Company
reason: Wood products and building-materials distribution driven by lumber/plywood/OSB prices and housing starts: EPS collapsed from $21.56 (2022) to $3.53 (0.16x peak) with EBIT margin 2.8%.

name: BioCryst Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
reason: Essentially a single-product rare-disease company (Orladeyo for HAE) that only turned profitable in 2025 after a decade of losses, facing new oral/injectable HAE competitors, shares up 11.6%/yr; the 18.6% LTM FCF yield is not yet a proven recurring base.

name: Brown-Forman Corporation
reason: Iconic brands (Jack Daniel's) but EPS CAGR only 1.0% over 10y and 0.71x its 2023 peak, with credible secular and policy threats (moderation/GLP-1 drinking declines, tariffs on American whiskey) and consensus EPS growth ~0-4% beyond FY1.

name: Black Hills Corporation
reason: Regulated electric/gas utility with EPS CAGR 3.2%, shares up 4.9%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 5.5x and negative FCF from capex; no route to 7%+ EPS growth and a pending NorthWestern merger adds transaction risk.
